fieldMarks: Moderately stout body with a moderately keeled tail, 6.4-12.7 cm total length.
Usually 6-8 pairs of golden spots on the back, which in adults may fuse into a light stripe with a dark, irregular border.
Wash of whitish or bluish speckling across sides and tail and no light-coloured 'portholes' on the flanks, separating it from several sympatric Desmognathus.
Nearly identical to northern dusky salamander; best told apart by range.
behavior: Takes refuge under logs, rocks and leaf litter by day and moves on stream banks at night.
Feeds opportunistically on small invertebrates, mostly terrestrial insects; may be active by day in dark, wet weather.
Females brood up to 35 eggs under moss or rocks from mid-June through August.
habitat: Floodplains, sloughs and mucky sites along upland streams to about 900 m, usually near running or trickling water.
Abundant in and near cool streams and small rivers in the Piedmont and lower mountains of SC and GA.
range: Lowland drainages east of the Mississippi River, from extreme southern Illinois and southwestern Kentucky to east-central Tennessee and northwest Georgia, south to the Florida Panhandle and west through Alabama and Louisiana. Not in Canada.

lookalikes.name: Northern dusky salamander
lookalikes.howToTell: Very similar; best separated by range (northern dusky is the northeastern species).
